_meta.source: Route structures from MOE, ITE and polytechnic progression information. No named individual appears in this file.
_meta.notes: Two kinds of card, and the app renders them differently on purpose. A profile card is a real named person from a published source, with the link on the card. A typical path card is a pattern built from how the system actually works, labelled as a pattern and never as a person. The profiles array is deliberately empty. The session that built this file had no network access to news outlets or to MOE and SkillsFuture feature pages, so no real profile could be verified. Rather than invent someone, the app ships with none and handles the empty case. Filling this array is the first item in OPEN_QUESTIONS.md.

typicalPaths.label: The long climb
typicalPaths.body: Starts at ITE with results that felt like bad news at sixteen. Each step is a real qualification that stands on its own. Between Higher Nitec and polytechnic there is a specific number to aim at: a GPA of 2.5 is the minimum from the 2027 intake, and 3.5 or above guarantees a place.
typicalPaths.takes: Eight years or so to a degree, with paid work available at every stage.
typicalPaths.whatMattered: Knowing the guarantee existed early enough to aim at it.

typicalPaths.label: Straight into the field
typicalPaths.body: Picks a field at seventeen, spends three years doing it, leaves with a portfolio and an internship on the record. Some go on to a degree with exemptions. Many do not, and do well anyway.
typicalPaths.takes: Three years to a qualification and a first job.
typicalPaths.whatMattered: Choosing a course they were actually interested in rather than the one with the highest cut off they could reach.

typicalPaths.label: The extra year
typicalPaths.body: Comes up short at the end of Sec 4, takes a fifth year to offer subjects at a more demanding level, and goes on with a wider set of options than they had. This route exists in the system precisely so that one set of results does not settle everything.
typicalPaths.takes: One extra year, invisible within a decade.
typicalPaths.whatMattered: Treating the year as a run up rather than a punishment.

typicalPaths.label: The switch
typicalPaths.body: Trains in one thing, works in it, and moves into something unrelated in their thirties or forties. From age 40 this is directly supported: a $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top up, a monthly training allowance worth half their income while studying full time, and up to 90 percent off a full time diploma.
typicalPaths.takes: One to three years to retrain, mid career.
typicalPaths.whatMattered: That they had kept learning something the whole way through, so the switch was a step and not a leap.

typicalPaths.label: Admitted on what they made
shape: Arts diploma, then practice or a degree
typicalPaths.body: Results were ordinary. The portfolio was not. Admission to the arts institutions and several polytechnic courses turns on aptitude and evidence of what you have actually done, through portfolios, auditions and the Early Admissions Exercise.
typicalPaths.whatMattered: Starting to make things at thirteen, before anyone told them it counted.

typicalPaths.label: The route people picture
typicalPaths.body: The route most familiar to parents, and a good one for people who like abstraction, argument and going deep on a few subjects. It is one route among several, and it is not the destination it is sometimes treated as.
typicalPaths.takes: Two years to A Levels, then three or four to a degree.
typicalPaths.whatMattered: Liking the way JC actually works, rather than choosing it because it sounded correct.
